podcast.title: Extreme Rarity of Single
podcast.body: The 7-inch single, "Your Furniture was always dead, I was just afraid to tell you," is incredibly rare, with only an estimated 100 copies produced and a mere two discovered. Its scarcity is such that major record collecting websites do not even attempt to price it, and audio recordings are nearly impossible to find online. "Only two of those 100 or so copies have been found so far. It is so rare that most record collecting sites won't even affix a price to it. I can't even find audio of it posted anywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Single Distribution
podcast.body: The Upholsterers famously hid about 100 vinyl copies of their 3-track 7-inch single, "Your Furniture was always dead, I was just afraid to tell you," inside furniture they were reupholstering. This unique distribution method contributed to the single's extreme rarity, with only two copies having been found. "Jack and Brian hid some singles inside couches and chairs that they were fixing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Apprenticeship and Punk Rock Exposure
xref.body: At age 15, Jack White (then Jack Gillis) became an apprentice to Brian Moldun, an upholsterer who exposed him to a wide range of punk rock music, significantly broadening his musical scope. This mentorship led to their musical collaboration as The Upholsterers. "When he was 15, Jack became an apprentice to a guy named Brian Moldun, who ran a place that re-apholstered furniture. While they were working, he exposed Jack to all kinds of punk rock, greatly expanding Jack's musical horizons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hidden Singles
xref.body: As part of an interesting twist for The Upholsterers project, Jack White and Brian Moldun hid approximately 100 vinyl copies of a 3-track 7-inch single, "Your Furniture was always dead, I was just afraid to tell you," inside couches and chairs they were reupholstering. As of the transcript, only two of these extremely rare copies have been found. "Jack and Brian hid some singles inside couches and chairs that they were fixing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Instrument Switch
xref.body: Jack White initially wanted to play drums in The Upholsterers, but since that was Brian Moldun's role, Jack switched to guitar, which would later become his signature instrument. "Jack wanted to play drums, but that was Brian's job, so Jack switched to guitar, and they actually recorded an album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Upholstery Background and Taxidermy Hobby
xref.body: Before breaking into the music business, Jack White was an apprentice upholsterer. He even formed a band with his boss called "The Upholsterers," and they recorded an album. More recently, Jack has taken up taxidermy. "In fact, he wasn't apprentice of poster her before he broke into the music business."
